title: Grateful Dead Live at Bob Marley Performing Arts Center on 1982-11-26
source: lineage: MSC(Sony TCD-5M) > WAV > SHNrecording:MSC - master soundboard cassette w/ Dolby B by Frank Streeterdigital transfer:Nakamichi CD 2 cassette deck > HHB 850 Pro stand-alone CD burner (16 bit @ 44.1khz) by Frank Streeter and Henry Fishertracking and

ai_review.summary: Pristine soundboard capture of the Montego Bay sunrise set, highlighted by a smoking Scarlet > Fire and soaring Fire on the Mountain.
ai_review.review: The gd82‑11‑26.sbd.streeter recording delivers clear, well‑balanced soundboard audio (with only minor pitch‑correction needs) that lets listeners hear the band’s tight playing despite the pre‑dawn hour.  The show is remembered for its breathtaking sunrise moment during Scarlet / Fire and a fiery Fire on the Mountain, with Brent’s Hammond work and Phil’s bass adding extra sparkle; opinions on the rest of the set are split, ranging from “underrated” to “average.”

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the performance (especially Scarlet/Fire and Fire on the Mountain) and note good soundboard quality; a minority label the show as weak, pulling the overall average to about four stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, crisp mix with occasional speed/pitch issues (needs ~‑2% repitch) and minor surface noise; far superior to cassette copies.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A short, compact set (6‑song first set) that builds into a sunrise second half; the transition from Scarlet into Fire at dawn is frequently cited as magical.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone and vocals are praised, especially during the sunrise Fire on the Mountain and his responsive lead work throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass is noted for stepping forward in the mix with funkier lines; some reviewers call it ‘fun’ and ‘bombing.’
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s Hammond organ is highlighted as “ripping” and “tremendous,” adding a lush texture to the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey and Bill receive special mention for an intense drum performance on Fire; overall drumming is described as tight and powerful.
